extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researching, crafting, and balancing historical accuracy with storytelling when writing historical fiction novels or long-form stories. Covers research sources, character and setting authenticity, language, cultural sensitivity, and avoiding common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance historical accuracy and storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Strike the right balance between getting facts right (historical accuracy) and exercising creative freedom (storytelling); avoid turning the novel into a textbook or making it feel unauthentic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much focus on historical detail can read like a textbook; too little can make the setting feel fake. Aim to let the story remain front and center while using historical detail to enrich and ground the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough research using primary and secondary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a solid research foundation using primary sources (letters, diaries, newspapers) to understand firsthand life and secondary sources (history books, academic articles) for analysis and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary sources help with how people thought, spoke, and lived; secondary sources provide interpretation and broader context. Use both types to form an authentic picture of the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate research naturally into the narrative (avoid info-dumps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weave historical detail into plot, character action, and dialogue rather than pausing the story to provide exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the layout of a city through a character’s journey or reveal social norms via dialogue and interactions. Anti-pattern: long expository paragraphs that halt plot momentum. Keep details incidental and organic to scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make research serve the story
rubrics_metrics.description: Use historical detail to support mood, character, and theme rather than showcasing research for its own sake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose details that enrich the reader’s experience and advance story or character development. If a fact doesn’t serve the narrative, consider leaving it out or minimizing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create characters authentic to their era
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure characters’ beliefs, behaviors, and speech reflect the social norms and lived realities of the time period, even when they are fictional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research societal norms and language nuances to inform mannerisms and dialogue. Fictional protagonists give flexibility, but their internal logic and outward behavior should be plausible for their era.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat setting as a character
rubrics_metrics.description: Recreate past worlds vividly — architecture, clothing, transportation, smells, and sounds — and let setting actively shape scenes and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select evocative details (e.g., the clatter and steam of an early industrial city) rather than exhaustive inventories. Use setting details to create atmosphere and influence plot or character choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance factual events with fictional elements plausibly
rubrics_metrics.description: When altering timelines or fictionalizing events, make creative liberties feel seamless and logical within the established historical world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tweaks to history are acceptable in fiction but should not break plausibility within the story’s internal logic. Signal or contextualize major changes so readers can accept them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid anachronisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent elements that are out of place for the period (modern phrases, technology, attitudes) from entering the text and disrupting immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use meticulous research and careful proofreading. Employ knowledgeable beta readers or experts to spot inaccuracies. Anachronisms are a common pitfall that can jolt readers out of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use period-appropriate language while maintaining readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture the flavor of the period in dialogue and narration without using language so archaic it becomes unreadable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ period-appropriate vocabulary and sentence rhythms but avoid obscure or overly archaic words that confuse modern readers. Aim for the 'essence' of the era rather than literal historical speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity and respectful portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray historical peoples, cultures, and social norms accurately without endorsing or glossing over harmful attitudes; be empathetic and nuanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge complexities of the past and avoid reproducing stereotypes or uncritical romanticization. Research marginalized perspectives and consider consultation with cultural experts when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on universal human elements to connect with modern readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor stories in emotions and themes (love, loss, ambition, conflict) that resonate across time to make the historical setting relatable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizing characters’ emotional journeys helps bridge past and present and keeps readers engaged despite temporal distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select which historical details to highlight vs. background
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberately choose which elements of the past to emphasize and which to leave implicit, so the narrative remains focused and immersive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight details that advance theme, character, or plot; relegate routine or irrelevant facts to background texture. This helps prevent overload and preserves pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use expert readers and knowledgeable beta readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlist experts or well-informed beta readers to identify inaccuracies, anachronisms, and insensitive portrayals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External readers can catch subtle errors and cultural blind spots the author may miss. Incorporate their feedback during revision to strengthen authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the story accessible to contemporary audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the narrative and themes remain readable and relevant to modern readers without compromising historical integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on modern-relevant themes and clear storytelling. Avoid heavy-handed periodizing that alienates readers; make the stakes and characters’ emotions intelligible today.
